title: Jack and the Beanstalk
source: English fairy tale (Joseph Jacobs, 1890, public domain). Original retelling.
moral: Be brave, be kind, and always come home to the people who love you.

pages.text: Once upon a time, a boy named Jack lived with his mother in a tiny house.
pages.caption: Jack and his mother

pages.text: They had one cow. Her name was Milky-White. Moo!
pages.caption: Milky-White the cow

pages.text: One day the cupboard was empty. "Jack," said his mother, "please take Milky-White to market."
pages.caption: Off to market

pages.text: On the road Jack met a funny old man. "I will trade you five magic beans for your cow."
pages.caption: Five magic beans

pages.text: Jack loved magic. So he said yes! He ran home with the beans in his pocket.
pages.caption: Yes, please!

pages.text: His mother was not happy. "Beans? Oh, Jack!" She tossed them out of the window.
pages.caption: Out the window

pages.text: In the morning, Jack looked outside. A giant beanstalk had grown up, up, up into the clouds!
pages.caption: Up, up, up!

pages.text: Jack climbed and climbed. Higher than the birds. Higher than the clouds.
pages.caption: Climb, Jack, climb

pages.text: At the top was a big, big castle. Jack tiptoed to the door. Knock, knock!
pages.caption: A giant castle

pages.text: Inside lived a giant. "Fee, fi, fo, fum!" he boomed. Jack hid behind a big brown pot.
pages.caption: Fee, fi, fo, fum!

pages.text: The giant had a hen. When the hen sat down, she laid an egg made of gold!
pages.caption: The golden egg

pages.text: Soon the giant fell asleep. Snore! Snore! Jack picked up the hen very, very gently.
pages.caption: Shh, he is sleeping

pages.text: Jack ran to the beanstalk and slid all the way down. Wheee!
pages.caption: Wheee!

pages.text: The giant woke up and stomped after him. Stomp! Stomp! But he was much too big to climb down.
pages.caption: Stomp, stomp!

pages.text: Jack fetched an axe. Chop, chop, chop! Down came the beanstalk, and the giant stayed up in the clouds forever.
pages.caption: Chop, chop, chop

pages.text: The little hen laid golden eggs every day. Jack and his mother never went hungry again.
pages.caption: Golden eggs every day

pages.text: And Jack was always brave, always kind, and always home for supper. The end.
pages.caption: Home for supper
